title: 67. Numeracy & Number Systems: Recognizing Prime and Composite Numbers
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a prime number from a pair of numbers.
questions.question: Which number is prime?
questions.explanation: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive divisors: \(1\) and itself. The number \(13\) is divisible only by \(1\) and \(13\), so it is prime. The number \(15\) is divisible by \(1\), \(3\), \(5\), and \(15\), so it is composite. Therefore, \(13\) is prime.
questions.hint: Check whether the number has any factor other than \(1\) and itself.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a composite number from a pair of numbers.
questions.question: Which number is composite?
questions.explanation: A composite number has more than two positive divisors. The number \(21\) is divisible by \(1\), \(3\), \(7\), and \(21\), so it is composite. The number \(17\) is divisible only by \(1\) and \(17\), so it is prime. Therefore, \(21\) is composite.
questions.hint: Look for a number that has a factor other than \(1\) and itself.

questions.concept: Numbers That Are Neither Prime nor Composite
questions.learningObjective: Identify a number that is neither prime nor composite.
questions.question: Which number is neither prime nor composite?
questions.explanation: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive divisors, and a composite number has more than two. The number \(1\) has only one positive divisor, namely \(1\), so it is neither prime nor composite. The number \(2\) has exactly two divisors, \(1\) and \(2\), so it is prime. Therefore, \(1\) is neither prime nor composite.
questions.hint: Count the positive divisors of each candidate and compare with the definitions.

questions.concept: Identifying Prime Numbers with Larger Values
questions.learningObjective: Determine which of two two-digit numbers is prime.
questions.question: Which number is prime?
questions.explanation: Check for divisors. The number \(51\) is divisible by \(3\) because \(5+1=6\), and \(51=3\times 17\), so \(51\) is composite. The number \(53\) is not divisible by \(2\), \(3\), \(5\), or \(7\), and \(\sqrt{53}<8\), so \(53\) has no divisor other than \(1\) and itself. Therefore, \(53\) is prime.
questions.hint: Test divisibility by small primes up to the square root of the number.

questions.concept: Identifying Composite Numbers with Larger Values
questions.learningObjective: Determine which of two two-digit numbers is composite.
questions.question: Which number is composite?
questions.explanation: The number \(91\) can be factored as \(91=7\times 13\), so it has divisors other than \(1\) and \(91\). Therefore, \(91\) is composite. The number \(97\) is not divisible by \(2\), \(3\), \(5\), or \(7\), and \(\sqrt{97}<10\), so \(97\) is prime. Thus, \(91\) is composite.
questions.hint: Try factoring the number using small prime divisors.

questions.concept: Counting Prime Numbers in an Interval
questions.learningObjective: Count how many prime numbers lie between 20 and 30.
questions.question: How many prime numbers are between \(20\) and \(30\)?
questions.explanation: List the integers between \(20\) and \(30\): \(21\), \(22\), \(23\), \(24\), \(25\), \(26\), \(27\), \(28\), \(29\). The numbers \(23\) and \(29\) have no divisors other than \(1\) and themselves, so they are prime. All the other numbers in this interval are composite. Therefore, there are \(2\) prime numbers between \(20\) and \(30\).
questions.hint: List the numbers in the interval and test each one for primality.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a list in which every number is prime.
questions.question: Which list contains only prime numbers?
questions.explanation: Check each number in both lists. In the list "\(2\), \(5\), \(9\)", \(2\) and \(5\) are prime, but \(9\) is composite because \(9=3\times 3\). In the list "\(3\), \(7\), \(11\)", \(3\), \(7\), and \(11\) are each divisible only by \(1\) and themselves, so all three are prime. Therefore, the list "\(3\), \(7\), \(11\)" contains only prime numbers.
questions.hint: Check every number in each list for factors other than \(1\) and itself.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a composite number that is a perfect square.
questions.question: Which number is composite?
questions.explanation: The number \(121\) is a perfect square because \(121=11\times 11\), so it has divisors \(1\), \(11\), and \(121\). Therefore, \(121\) is composite. The number \(113\) is not divisible by \(2\), \(3\), \(5\), or \(7\), and \(\sqrt{113}<11\), so \(113\) is prime. Thus, \(121\) is composite.
questions.hint: Look for a number that can be written as a product of two equal factors greater than \(1\).

questions.concept: Combining Primality and a Digit-Sum Condition
questions.learningObjective: Identify a prime that also satisfies a given digit condition.
questions.question: Which number is prime and has digit sum \(10\)?
questions.explanation: The digit sum of \(73\) is \(7+3=10\). Testing primes up to \(\sqrt{73}<9\), none of \(2\), \(3\), \(5\), \(7\) divides \(73\), so it is prime. Although \(79\) is also prime, its digit sum is \(16\), so it fails the stated condition.
questions.hint: Check the digit condition and primality separately.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which of two three-digit numbers is composite.
questions.question: Which number is composite?
questions.explanation: The number \(143\) can be factored as \(143=11\times 13\), so it has divisors other than \(1\) and \(143\). Therefore, \(143\) is composite. The number \(139\) is not divisible by \(2\), \(3\), \(5\), \(7\), or \(11\), and \(\sqrt{139}<12\), so \(139\) is prime. Thus, \(143\) is composite.
questions.hint: Test divisibility by small primes up to the square root of each number.
